basis: Macroglossia, omphalocele and somatic overgrowth characterize this subtype; transient neonatal hypoglycemia and tumour predisposition do not establish additional organ damage.
N-glycosylation defect with universal developmental impairment; hearing and visual impairment each occur in 30-79%. Gastric bleeding is less consistently documented across patients.
Spastic paraplegia and peripheral neuropathy define this phospholipid-metabolism disorder; no additional organ has established common direct damage.
Developmental delay, ataxia and tremor define the syndrome; esotropia occurs in 3/4 and scoliosis in 2/4 reported patients.
Ichthyosis and microcephaly with tetraplegia define the syndrome. Nonspecific muscle abnormalities do not establish independent skeletal muscle damage.
Chronic inflammatory airway disease with aspirin-triggered severe obstruction; immune-mediated airway inflammation is intrinsic to the disease.
Life-threatening inflammatory asthma with respiratory arrest or ventilatory failure; hypercapnia and altered consciousness do not establish additional organ damage.
Tyrosine metabolism defect with acidosis; fine sparse hair in 80-99%; intellectual disability and microcephaly each reported in 1/3, supporting borderline neurologic involvement.
Inherited protein C deficiency is a coagulation disorder; thromboses are separately diagnosed complications, and warfarin skin necrosis is treatment-related.
Umbrella category defined by viral infection and sexual transmission; no single anatomical organ is consistently damaged across its subtypes.
Osteopetrosis and neuroaxonal disease with cerebral atrophy and callosal agenesis define the syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in only 5-29%.
Sudden cessation of cardiac activity defines the disease; hypoxic injury to other organs is not universally established by this concept.
Adrenal cortisol excess causes myopathy/bone loss (~50-80%), skin atrophy/striae (~50-70%) and hypertension (~70-85%); estimates derive from overt Cushing syndrome.
Inherited keratinization disorder with palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, abnormal hair, nails and sweating; all documented manifestations fall within skin and its appendages.
Carcinoma originates in both breasts; breast has no axis, and metastatic disease is not specified.
GABRB1-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; cerebral visual impairment originates in the brain and does not establish ocular disease.
Neoplasm of the hematopoietic/lymphoid system involving lymph nodes; the umbrella includes non-lymphoma tumours, so an immune mechanism is not assumed.
Carcinoma originates in the external ear, which is explicitly covered by the otologic axis.
Inflammation is localized to a congenital diverticulum of the small intestine; infection or an immune-mediated mechanism is not established.
Inherited oxalate-handling disorder with hyperoxaluria, calcium oxalate stones, obstruction and acute kidney injury in the reported patient.
Corynebacterium diphtheriae infection of anterior nasal structures; the nose belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Severe skeletal myopathy with reducing bodies; respiratory insufficiency in 2/2 results from respiratory muscle weakness and does not establish intrinsic lung disease.
Mechanical outward displacement of the eyelid; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.
Muscle atrophy, delayed skeletal maturation and lipoatrophy define the phenotype; cataract occurs in 1/3. Hepatocellular carcinoma is a separate predisposed malignancy.
Malignant neoplasm originates in the urinary bladder dome; the bladder belongs to the renal axis.
